bull.b: Expansion beyond the historical residential base broadens NeoVolta’s addressable market and reduces reliance on one customer segment. Serving commercial, industrial, and utility-scale applications could support a more diversified revenue base as the company develops products and converts its pipeline.

A domestic production footprint and stated FEOC compliance position can improve eligibility for customers requiring domestic content and regulatory alignment. This capability may strengthen NeoVolta’s competitiveness in procurement processes and support longer-term access to U.S. storage demand.

The five-year SK On agreement provides a defined source of U.S.-manufactured LFP cells across the planned production period. That relationship supports manufacturing scale-up, reinforces domestic-content capabilities, and gives NeoVolta a foundation for pursuing larger storage deployments.

bear.b: A collapse to zero reported revenue indicates that commercialization has not yet become reliable, despite prior growth. Such volatility makes planning difficult, weakens operating leverage, and raises the risk that facility investments and expanded capabilities remain underutilized over the next several quarters.

Widening losses show that NeoVolta’s current cost base is materially ahead of realized revenue and that scale benefits have not yet emerged. Continued losses can consume capital needed for production execution, increase financing dependence, and delay the point at which the business can self-fund growth.

Accelerating cash burn means NeoVolta remains dependent on external financing while it works to restore revenue and reduce losses. This limits financial flexibility, increases sensitivity to funding conditions, and could constrain investment or operations if the planned ramp takes longer than expected.
